extraction.name: TOFU
extraction.description: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. A benchmark dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, used to evaluate the efficacy of unlearning algorithms.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.citeAs: Maini, P., Feng, Z., Schwarzschild, A., Lipton, Z. C., & Kolter, J. Z. (2024). TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is composed entirely of fictitious author biographies synthesized by GPT-4. It is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes (seed data).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Predefined attributes (seed data) such as birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and parents’ professions. Book title keywords were seeded using the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: An elaborate prompt was used that deterministically seeds various author attributes to minimize the risk of confounders leaking from pretraining data. Keywords from two books from each genre were randomly selected from the Goodreads dataset to seed book titles.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: GPT-4 was tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author based on the seeded attributes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Initial experimentation without seeding attributes resulted in biases (e.g., repeated words like 'tides' and 'shadows', birth years concentrated in 1975). Seeding attributes led to significantly more diverse data based on manual inspection and word frequency analysis.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, parents’ professions
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Addresses legal and ethical concerns regarding LLMs memorizing and reproducing sensitive or private data. Simulates the practical scenario of the Right to be Forgotten, which is critical to LLM deployment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Initial generation without seeding showed biases towards specific birth years (1970-1980, especially 1975), book titles containing words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', 'whispers', and similar upbringings/writing styles ('magical'). These were mitigated by seeding attributes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark task is limited to unlearning information learned during finetuning, not pretraining. The forget quality metric may be gamed by models outputting gibberish. The scope of benchmarked unlearning methods is limited to those with O(number of samples) compute. It focuses on entity-level forgetting, not instance-level or behavior-level.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the efficacy of machine unlearning algorithms (Training, Testing).
